storyTemplate.title: Borderlands: The First Vault Hunt
storyTemplate.description: A source-faithful EmberAdventures retelling of Borderlands, covering the base-game Vault Hunt from Marcus's bus stop outside Fyrestone through Nine-Toes, Sledge, Dahl Headlands, New Haven, Tannis, Crazy Earl, Krom, Jaynistown, the Rakk Hive, Baron Flynt, Commandant Steele, and the Destroyer.

story_source.title: Borderlands
story_source.description: Retelling of the first Borderlands video game base campaign only, starting when Marcus drops the selected Vault Hunter outside Fyrestone.
story_source.modifications: EmberAdventures adaptation with selectable original Vault Hunters at start. DLC and later Borderlands titles are excluded unless the user asks.

meta.canon_scope_lock: Borderlands base-game campaign only. Do not include DLC or later-series content unless the user explicitly expands the scope.

pandora.name: Pandora
pandora.summary: A violent frontier planet rumored to hide an alien Vault.

detail.description: Pandora is dry, dangerous, corporate-abandoned, full of bandits, skags, Eridian ruins, gun vending machines, and people willing to kill for a rumor.

arid-badlands.name: Arid Badlands
arid-badlands.summary: The starting desert region around Fyrestone.

detail.description: Dusty roads, skag dens, bandit camps, broken Dahl machinery, and Fyrestone's first jobs define the opening arc.

fyrestone-bus-stop.name: Fyrestone Bus Stop
fyrestone-bus-stop.summary: The dusty road where Marcus drops off the selected Vault Hunter.

detail.description: A cracked asphalt pullout, a weather-beaten Fyrestone sign, heat shimmer, and CL4P-TP waiting too cheerfully.
A rusted gate and scrap walls mark the first push from bus stop into town.

fyrestone.name: Fyrestone
fyrestone.summary: A harsh little settlement that becomes the first hub.

detail.description: Fyrestone is a tiny outpost of scrap walls, vending machines, Dr. Zed's clinic, and immediate trouble.

fyrestone-yard.name: Fyrestone Yard
fyrestone-yard.summary: The first usable hub area inside Fyrestone.

detail.description: The town yard connects the clinic, bounty board, vending machines, and routes out into skag and bandit country.

dr-zeds-clinic.name: Dr. Zed's Clinic
dr-zeds-clinic.summary: A rough clinic and early mission hub.

detail.description: A grimy medical shack where Zed gives the Vault Hunter work and access to the local survival loop.

skag-gully.name: Skag Gully
skag-gully.summary: A skag-filled canyon where Nine-Toes waits.

detail.description: Bone piles, dens, and bandit signs turn the canyon into the first real named-boss route.

tk-bahas-farm.name: T.K. Baha's Farm
tk-bahas-farm.summary: T.K. Baha's lonely farm outside Fyrestone.

detail.description: A fragile farmstead surrounded by skag trouble, bandit cruelty, and T.K.'s grim jokes.

bone-heads-camp.name: Bone Head's Camp
bone-heads-camp.summary: The camp holding the stolen Catch-A-Ride module.

detail.description: A bandit roadblock camp where Bone Head controls a critical piece of vehicle tech.

arid-hills.name: Arid Hills
arid-hills.summary: The road toward Shep Sanders and Sledge's territory.

detail.description: Dry travel lanes, wind turbines, and bad roads carry the hunt toward Sledge.

sledge-safe-house.name: Sledge's Safe House
sledge-safe-house.summary: A bandit-held site tied to Sledge's mine key.

detail.description: Sledge's men guard the route and information needed to reach Headstone Mine.
A brutal industrial mine converted into Sledge's fortress and the end of the Fyrestone arc.

dahl-headlands.name: Dahl Headlands
dahl-headlands.summary: A vehicle-heavy desert region after Fyrestone.

detail.description: Long dusty roads, bandit racers, Lucky's garage, and broken fast-travel infrastructure widen the campaign.
A rough mechanic outpost where the Vault Hunter gets the region moving again.
New Haven is a better-defended settlement led by Helena Pierce, linking the Vault Hunt to Tannis and the Rust Commons.

rust-commons-west.name: Rust Commons West
rust-commons-west.summary: The western Rust Commons and Tannis route.

detail.description: Research sites, old wreckage, and dangerous errands make the Vault Hunt more explicitly Eridian.
Scrap walls, barking paranoia, and payment in disgusting favors block the next lead.

rust-commons-east.name: Rust Commons East
rust-commons-east.summary: The eastern Rust Commons route to Krom, Jaynistown, and Trash Coast.

detail.description: Bandit power, company-town betrayal, and key-piece hunts crowd this part of the campaign.
High catwalks, turret fire, and entrenched bandits protect one Vault Key piece.

jaynistown.name: Jaynistown
jaynistown.summary: A town tangled in the Kobb family conflict.

detail.description: The Vault Hunter is drawn through apparent errands and into Jaynistown's violent political reversal.

trash-coast.name: Trash Coast
trash-coast.summary: The coastal route to the Rakk Hive.

detail.description: Open ground, cliffs, and swarms build toward the Rakk Hive fight.

old-haven.name: Old Haven
old-haven.summary: A ruined town under Crimson Lance pressure.

detail.description: Old Haven marks the campaign's shift from bandit chaos to a military race against the Crimson Lance.
Salt roads and bandit strongholds lead toward Baron Flynt and the final key-piece chase.

the-back-door.name: The Back Door
the-back-door.summary: The hidden late-game route beyond the Salt Flats.

detail.description: A hard approach into the final fortress path after Baron Flynt.

crimson-fastness.name: Crimson Fastness
crimson-fastness.summary: A Crimson Lance fortress blocking the final pursuit.

detail.description: Military corridors, communications systems, and Lance resistance stand between the Vault Hunter and Steele.

eridian-promontory.name: Eridian Promontory
eridian-promontory.summary: The final alien route to the Vault.

detail.description: Eridian structures and Guardians reveal that the Vault is not a normal treasure room.
The campaign's destination, hiding the Destroyer instead of simple loot.

fyrestone-coliseum.name: Fyrestone Coliseum
fyrestone-coliseum.summary: The early Circle of Death arena.

detail.description: A local arena chain for players who want more combat before Sledge.

scene.summary: Marcus has just dropped the selected Vault Hunter outside Fyrestone. CL4P-TP is present and trying to lead the way into town.

story_rules.text: Use only Borderlands base-game campaign material unless the user explicitly asks to add DLC or later-series content.
Only the selected Vault Hunter is the player character at the start. Do not place the other selectable Vault Hunters in the scene unless play explicitly introduces them later.
Do not invent placeholder NPCs for locked future-cast roles. When a role is about to matter, unlock the predefined source character through the objective reward.
Offer optional side objectives when their region and prerequisite make sense, but do not force them ahead of the main Vault Hunt.

world_notes: The campaign starts at Marcus's bus stop outside Fyrestone with CL4P-TP present.

The source backbone is the first Borderlands game: Fyrestone, Nine-Toes, T.K. Baha, Catch-A-Ride, Sledge, Dahl Headlands, New Haven, Tannis, Earl, Krom, Jaynistown, Rakk Hive, Old Haven, Salt Flats, Crimson Lance, Steele, the Vault, and the Destroyer.
Borderlands should feel dry, dangerous, loot-driven, and darkly funny without turning into abstract meta comedy.
unresolved_threads: The Vault Hunt has not truly begun; the Vault Hunter only knows the rumor and has just arrived.
rules_and_constraints: Do not use Borderlands DLC or later-title content unless the user requests it.
Future cast should be introduced by objectives, not leaked by objective titles before the unlock.
Use real source names for NPCs and bosses; never generate generic role names like Bandit Leader as a permanent NPC name.
major_later_beats: Fyrestone opening: bus stop, Claptrap guide, Dr. Zed, skags, and Nine-Toes.
Arid Badlands expansion: T.K. Baha, Catch-A-Ride, Bone Head, Shep Sanders, Sledge's Safe House, and Headstone Mine.
Dahl Headlands and New Haven: Lucky Zaford, fast travel infrastructure, vehicle combat, Mad Mel, Helena Pierce, and a larger hub.
Tannis and Rust Commons: research journals, Crazy Earl, Krom's Canyon, Jaynistown, and Trash Coast.
Endgame: Rakk Hive, Old Haven, Salt Flats, Baron Flynt, Crimson Fastness, Commandant Steele, Eridian Promontory, the Vault, and the Destroyer.

Optional side branches include T.K.'s personal errands, Moe and Marley, Circle of Death, Claptrap rescues, Death Race Pandora, Tannis journals, Crazy Earl errands, Bandit Treasure, and Old Haven smoke signals.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text:
Marcus's bus coughs dust into the road and pulls away, leaving the selected Vault Hunter under the hard Pandora sun.

Fyrestone squats ahead behind rusted scrap walls. Skag bones bleach beside the cracked asphalt. A small yellow robot pivots on one wheel and throws both metal arms into the air.

(CL4P-TP) "Welcome to Fyrestone! I am CL4P-TP, your designated steward bot! Please ignore any rumors of bandits, skags, sudden death, or paperwork! Follow me, and I will almost certainly not lead you into immediate danger!"

CL4P-TP wobbles toward the gate, waving the Vault Hunter after him.
